text.title: Constitution Admission Routing
text.summary: Routing for ONE candidate rule. Run it per candidate, not per file. Most candidates leave — that is the gate working, not the gate being too strict.

decision-tree.root-question: For this one candidate: is it durable beyond the current feature, cross-cutting beyond one module, contestable by a competent engineer, and checkable by a named observation?

conclusion.verdict: Route to project-spec/. Domain facts change on a different clock from working agreements; admitting one drags that churn into a file that is meant to be stable and always loaded.
Route to roadmap.md. A target is not a constraint on how work is done, and it expires on a date rather than on an amendment.
Route to decisions.md or an ADR. That is the append-only history. If the choice also imposes a standing constraint, admit the CONSTRAINT here as a rule and leave the reasoning there.
Route to that module's AGENTS.md. Local conventions are read by whoever opens the module; putting them here taxes every phase in the project for the benefit of one directory.
Drop it. 'Write tests', 'keep code clean' — if no competent engineer would choose otherwise, the rule carries no information and costs context on every load.

Not admissible as written. Either name the observation that would show a violation and rewrite around it, or drop it. An unfalsifiable rule cannot be cited in a review, which is the only place a rule does work.
Defer. Not understood well enough to bind anyone yet. Do NOT write it with a placeholder reason — a why backfilled later rationalises the rule instead of constraining it.

Admitted, but something must leave first: merge two overlapping rules, demote one to a module AGENTS.md, or retire one that no longer binds. Raising the cap is how the file becomes unloadable, and an unread rule is not a rule.
Admit it AND move the check into a linter, hook or CI job, then cite that job from the rule. Rules that a machine enforces should shrink the human-read set, not add to it.

Admit. Assign the next unused R-NN — never reuse a retired id — write the one-sentence why first, then the rule body in at most 60 words. Bump MINOR, update the Sync Impact Report and the footer dates.

Overlay, not alternative: amend or retire the existing rule in the same change. Never append a contradicting rule below the old one — a file holding both positions lets the reader pick the one that suits them. MAJOR bump if a rule is removed or reversed.
